newsitem.title: UK: BAA 9 mos profits at lower end of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: BAA 9 mos profits at lower end of forecasts.

text.p: UK airports group BAA Plc reported a 6.2 percent rise in nine month pretax profit on Monday to 397 million stg ($636.5 million) for the period ended December 31.

Total revenue stood at 1.06 billion stg versus 987 million, with 76.6 million passengers using the airports, a 4.4 percent rise on the preceding year. BAA said it had taken eight million pounds off profits in line with its four-year programme of phasing out the difference between peak and off-peak period passenger charges. This profit should be recovered in the fourth quarter, however, and so has a neutral impact in the year.

Revenue from airport and traffic charges stood at 385 million stg, up 5.5 percent. Retailing revenue from airport shops was up 10 percent at 475 million pounds producing net retail income of 331 million, a rise of 11 percent. Property income was up 8.4 percent to 168 million.

Sir John Egan, chief executive, welcomed the figures and said the company now faced a period of more certainty following the Civil Aviation Authority decision on the regulatory framework for the next five years.

The CAA published price controls of RPI (the retail price index) minus three percent last summer. It also said there was no need for the UK to split control of BAA's aiports which include the two biggest hubs Heathrow and Gatwick.
Earnings per share for the period was 28.9 pence per share versus 26.1 pence.
